newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-DAVENPORT BEATS RAYMOND TO WIN OKLAHOMA CITY TOURNAMENT.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-DAVENPORT BEATS RAYMOND TO WIN OKLAHOMA CITY TOURNAMENT.

text.p: Olympic champion Lindsay Davenport won for the first time since last August by beating Lisa Raymond 6-4 6-2 Sunday in the finals of the $164,250 IGA Tennis Classic.
The top-seeded, 20-year-old Californian received $27,000 for claiming her eighth career pro victory.
Davenport led the first set 5-4, but trailed 30-40 in the 10th game. She got the game to deuce and closed out the set with an ace.
She immediately broke Raymond's serve to open the second set as the fourth-seeded player had two double faults. Davenport stormed out to a 4-0 lead and was never headed.
"Winning that 5-4 game was huge," Davenport said. "If it gets to 5-5, it would have been such a difference.
"It is always important to get off to a good start any time and that was the case the second set."
Davenport, ranked eighth, has been struggling in recent months.
She won three tournaments in 1996, but nothing since winning the Olympics in Atlanta and a $450,000 tournament in Los Angeles.
"Things were really rolling for me, winning the Olympics and Los Angeles," Davenport said. "I think I got burned out. I was playing a lot of tennis."
""That's the reason I came here. I didn't play that well in Australia and wanted to get my confidence up. I think my game is just now back where it was."
Raymond, ranked 26th, battled back from a bout with the flu during the week to reach the finals of a tournament for only the fifth time in her career.

"I definitely needed to serve better," said Raymond, who received $13,500. "I needed to get a lot more first serves in. There's no way I could have played her the way I did in the semifinals (a 6-1 6-0 win over Francesca Lubiana of Italy).
